akhfash:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said ﴿تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِ﴾ with a light [sīn], because it is from their asking one another: it is "يَتَساءَلُونَ", and the latter tāʾ has been dropped. This is frequent in the speech of the Arabs, e.g. ﴿تَكَلَّمُونَ﴾. And if you wish you may make it heavy [i.e. doubled] by assimilating (idghām).
Allah the Exalted said ﴿وَٱلأَرْحَامَ﴾ — accusative (manṣūb), i.e. "fear [the severing of] the wombs (kinship)". Some read ﴿والأَرْحامِ﴾ in the genitive (jarr). The first is better, because you do not make an overt genitive noun follow (by conjunction) a genitive pronoun.
And [Allah the Exalted said ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيباً﴾]: from "الرقيب" (the watcher) you say "رَقَبَ", "يَرْقُبُ", "رَقْباً" and "رَقُوبا".

akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿وَلاَ تَأْكُلُوۤاْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلَىٰ أَمْوَالِكُمْ﴾, i.e. "together with (مَعَ) your wealth". ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوْباً كَبِيرا﴾ means: "devouring it is a great sin".

akhfash:3-3.t:
He said ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تُقْسِطُواْ فِي ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ﴾, because it is from "أَقْسَطَ", "يُقْسِطُ", and "الإِقْساطُ" is justice. As for "قَسَطَ", it means "he was unjust (جَار)". He said ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلْقَاسِطُونَ فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً﴾. So "أَقْسَطَ" is: he acted justly, and "قَسَطَ" is: he acted unjustly. He said ﴿وَأَقْسِطُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾.
He said ﴿مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تَعْدِلُواْ فَوَاحِدَةً﴾, meaning: "then marry one ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾", i.e. marry what your right hands possess. As for the absence of tanwīn (tark al-ṣarf, diptote treatment) in ﴿مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾, it is because they are diverted (maʿdūl) from "اثنين", "ثَلاث" and "أَربع", just as "عُمَر", being diverted from "عامِر", is not given tanwīn. And Allah the Exalted said ﴿أُوْلِيۤ أَجْنِحَةٍ مَّثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾, so it was put in the accusative [i.e. without tanwīn in the genitive]. And He said ﴿أَن تَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ مَثْنَىٰ وَفُرَادَىٰ﴾, and it is likewise diverted. If you named [someone] with it you would give it tanwīn, because when it is a name it does not carry the meaning of "two", "three" and "four" — just as one says "نَزَالِ" when it has the meaning of "dismount!", but when you name [someone] with it you put it in the nominative.
The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-second shāhid]:
أَحَمَّ اللّهُ ذلِكَ مِنْ لِقاءٍ * أُحادَ أُسادَ في شَهْرٍ حَلال
(May Allah bring about that encounter — one by one, [as] lions, in a month in which fighting is lawful.)
And he said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-third shāhid]:
وَلَكِنَّما أَهْلِي بِوادٍ أَنِيسُه * ذِئابٌ تَبَغَّى الناسَ مَثْنَى وَمْوحَدا
(But my people are in a valley whose only companions are wolves that seek out people two by two and one by one.)
And Allah the Exalted said ﴿فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾, meaning: "let each one of you marry each [woman] of this number", as Allah the Exalted said ﴿فَٱجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً﴾, meaning: "flog each one of them".

akhfash:4-4.t:
He said ﴿وَآتُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً﴾. The singular of "الصَّدُقاتِ" is صَدُقَة (dowry), and the Banū Tamīm [say] "صُدْقة", with the dāl unvowelled and the ṣād with ḍamma. [Translator's note: the text has «بنو عميم», evidently for Banū Tamīm.]
And He said ﴿فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَيْءٍ مِّنْهُ نَفْساً﴾: the singular may be treated like the plural, because He only meant "the inclination (الهَوى)", and "the inclination" may be collective. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-fourth shāhid]:
 بِها جِيَفُ الحَسْرى فأَمَّا عِظامُها * فَبِيضٌ وأمّا جِلْدُها فصَليبُ
(In it are the carcasses of the exhausted [camels]: as for their bones, they are white, and as for their skin, it is hard.) [i.e. "skin" in the singular for the plural.]
As for "هَنِيءٌ مَريءُ" (wholesome and pleasant), you say "هَنُؤَ هذا الطعام ومرؤ" and "هَنِىءَ ومَرِىءَ", as you say "فَقِهَ" and "فَقُهَ", giving the qāf kasra or ḍamma. And you say "هَنَأَنِي", "هنَئِتُهُ" and "استمرأته".

akhfash:6-6.t:
[And he said]** ﴿فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ رُشْداً﴾. He said ﴿آنَسْتُمْ﴾ with a long [alif]. You say "آنَسْتُ منهُ رُشْداً وخيراً" (I perceived in him sound judgement and good), and ﴿آنَسْتُ نَارا﴾ is like it, with a long [alif]. And you say "أنِسْتُ بالرَّجُلِ" "أُنْساً" (I was at ease with the man): the alif of "أَنِسْتُ" is short and the alif of "أُنْساً" has ḍamma*. And "أنَسَا" is also said.
And He said ﴿إِسْرَافاً وَبِدَاراً أَن يَكْبَرُواْ﴾, meaning: do not devour it, hastening before they grow up.

akhfash:7-7.t: He said ﴿لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصيِبٌ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلْوَالِدَانِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿نَصِيباً مَّفْرُوضاً﴾: its accusative is like the accusative of ﴿كِتَاباً مُّؤَجَّلاً﴾.

akhfash:8-8.t: He said ﴿وَإِذَا حَضَرَ ٱلْقِسْمَةَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينُ﴾, then He said ﴿فَٱرْزُقُوهُمْ مِّنْهُ﴾ [with a masculine pronoun], because its meaning is the wealth and the inheritance, so He used the masculine according to that meaning.

akhfash:9-9.t: He said ﴿وَلْيَخْشَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُواْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً﴾, because He means "let those fear who, if they left behind them offspring, would fear for them" the like of what they themselves see [being done to] the offspring of others. [Translator's note: the text has «يركون», apparently for «يرون» "they see".] That is: let them not do that, so that others do not do it to theirs. "فليخشوا", i.e. "let them fear this", i.e. let them be wary. Then He came back again and said "so let them fear Allah (فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللّهَ)".

akhfash:10-10.t: [And] He said ﴿سَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيراً﴾: the yāʾ here may take fatḥa or ḍamma, and both are correct. And His saying ﴿فِي بُطُونِهِمْ﴾ is tawkīd (emphasis).

akhfash:11-11.t:
He said ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيۤ أَوْلاَدِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ ٱلأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾. "مِثْل" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is only an explanation of the injunction, as He said ﴿وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾: He explained the promise, meaning "thus He promised them", i.e. He said "for them is forgiveness". The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-fifth shāhid]:
عَشِيَّةَ ما وَدَّ ابْنُ غَرَّاءَ أْمُّهُ * لَها مِنْ سِوانا إذْ دَعَا أَبَوانِ
(On the evening when the son of Gharrāʾ — his mother did not wish that she had parents other than us, when he called out.)
He said ﴿فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَاءً﴾: He left the first construction and said [in effect] "if those left behind are women", [with "women"] in the accusative; and likewise ﴿وَإِن كَانَتْ وَاحِدَةً﴾.
And He said ﴿وَلأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ﴾: this hāʾ in "أبويه" is the pronoun of the deceased, because when He said ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيۤ أَوْلاَدِكُمْ﴾ the meaning was: Allah enjoins the deceased before his death that he owes his parents such-and-such and his child such-and-such — i.e. let [each] take only what is his.
And He said ﴿فَإِن كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ﴾: they mention that "brothers" [here] means two; and like it is "إنّا فَعَلْنا" (we did) when you are two. What consists of two things may be likened [to a plural] though it is not the same as it; but two have been made a plural [in] the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿إِن تَتُوبَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾, and He said ﴿وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقْطَعُوۤاْ أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾. That is because in the speech of the Arabs any two things [taken] from two things are [treated as] a plural; and in poetry it may be dual. [The poet said]:
[in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-sixth shāhid]:
بِما فِي فُؤادَيْنا من الشَوْقِ والهَوى * فَيُجْبَرُ مُنْهاضُ الفُؤَادِ المُشَعَّفُ
(By the longing and passion in our two hearts, so that the broken, love-smitten heart may be mended.)
And al-Farazdaq said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-seventh shāhid]:
هُما نَفَثا فِي فِيَّ مِنْ فَمَوَيْهِما * على النّابِحِ العاوِي أَشَدّ لِجامِ
(The two of them breathed into my mouth from their two mouths the strongest bridle against the barking, howling one.)
And in poetry this may be made singular. He said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-eighth shāhid]:
لا نُنْكِرُ القَتْلَ وقد سُبِينا * في حَلْقِكُمْ عَظْمٌ وَقَدْ شُجِينا
(We do not deny the killing, and we have been taken captive; in your throat is a bone, and we have been choked.) [i.e. "throat" in the singular for the plural.]
And another said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and sixty-ninth shāhid]:
كُلُوا في بَعْضِ بَطْنِكُمُ تَعَفُّوا * فإِنَّ زَمانَخكُمْ زَمَنَ خَمِيصُ
(Eat in part of your belly and you will remain restrained, for your time is a time of hunger.) [Translator's note: «زَمانَخكُمْ» is evidently a typo in the source for «زَمانَكُمْ».]
Parallel to this is their saying "تِسْعُ مئة" (nine hundred), when it is really "تِسْعُ مئات" or "مِئيِن"; they made it singular. That is because [the counted noun] from three to ten is plural, e.g. "ثلاثة رجال" and "عشرةُ رجال", but then they made it singular with "hundreds".
And He said ﴿مِن بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِهَآ﴾ because He had mentioned the man when He said ﴿وَوَرِثَهُ أَبَواهُ﴾. Some read ﴿يُوصِى﴾ [with the passive], and both are good. And the parallel of ﴿يُوصِي﴾ with yāʾ [is in what follows].

akhfash:12-12.t:
﴿تُوْصُونَ﴾ and ﴿يُوصِينَ﴾ when He mentioned them [the women]. And the one who read ﴿يُوصِي﴾ with yāʾ argued from His saying ﴿غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّ وَصِيَّةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾. [So] ﴿وَصِيَّةً﴾ and ﴿فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ are put in the accusative just as ﴿كِتَاباً مُؤَجَّلاً﴾ is put in the accusative.
And He said ﴿وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلاَلَةً﴾. If it were read ﴿يُورِثُ﴾ it would be good, with ﴿كَلاَلَةً﴾ in the accusative; this has been reported from al-Ḥasan. If you wish, you put كلالةً in the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿كانَ﴾ and make ﴿يُورَث﴾ a qualifier of "the man"; and if you wish, you make ﴿كانَ﴾ dispense with a khabar, like "وَقَعَ" (it occurred), and make the accusative of ﴿كَلالَةً﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he is inherited from as a kalāla", as you say "يُضْرَبُ قَائِماً" (he is beaten while standing). The poet said, regarding the "kāna" that has no khabar [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and seventieth shāhid]:
فِدَى لِبَنِي ذُهْلِ بنِ شَيْبانَ نَاقَتِي * إذا كانَ يَوْمٌ ذُو كواكِبَ أشهَبُ
(My she-camel is a ransom for the Banū Dhuhl ibn Shaybān when there comes a grey day full of stars [i.e. a day of fierce battle].)
He said ﴿وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلاَلَةً أَو ٱمْرَأَةٌ وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا﴾: He means "of the two mentioned". And it is permissible for us to say of the man, when you have said "زيدٌ أو عمرٌ مُنْطَلِقٌ" (Zayd or ʿAmr is leaving): "هذانِ رجلا سَوْء" (these two are bad men), i.e. the two whom you mentioned.

akhfash:22-22.t: He said ﴿وَلاَ تَنكِحُواْ مَا نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾, because its meaning is: for you will be held to account for it; that is why He said ﴿إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾, i.e. then there is no blame on you. The like of this is frequent in the speech of the Arabs; you say "لا نَصْنَعْ ما صَنَعْتَ" (let us not do what you did) "ولا نَأْكُلْ ما أَكَلْتَ" (and let us not eat what you ate).

akhfash:25-25.t:
He said ﴿وَمَن لَّمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكُمْ طَوْلاً أَن يَنكِحَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَاتِ﴾ on the pattern of "whoever does not find the means to marry", meaning "إلى أنْ ينكِحَ" (towards marrying), because the preposition is left implied with "أن".
And He said ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ بَعْضُكُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ﴾, putting ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And He said ﴿بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ﴾, because "الأَهْل" (family) is a collective, but it may be pluralised, so one says "أَهْلُونَ", as you say "قَوْمٌ" and "أقوامٌ", pluralising the collective. He said ﴿شَغَلَتْنَآ أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا﴾, using the plural. And He said ﴿قُوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَاراً﴾: this yāʾ is the yāʾ of the plural, which is why it is unvowelled; thus its accusative and genitive have an unvowelled yāʾ, and the nūn has gone because of the iḍāfa (genitive construct).
And He said ﴿وَأَن تَصْبِرُواْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾, meaning: "and patience is better for you".
He said ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ بَعْضُكُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ﴾, i.e. Allah knows best the faith of some of you [in relation to] others.

akhfash:26-26.t: He said ﴿يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ﴾, meaning "وَلِيَهْدِيَكُمْ" (and to guide you); its meaning is: He wills such-and-such in order to make clear to you. And if you wish, you may take it that the verb is connected by the lām to "أن", which is implied after the lām, as in ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ﴾, and as He said ﴿وَأُمِرْتُ لأعْدِلَ بَيْنَكُمُ﴾, with the lām given kasra, i.e. I have been commanded for the sake of that.

akhfash:29-29.t: He said ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنْكُمْ﴾. His saying ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَارَةٌ﴾ is an exception outside [the scope of] the beginning of the speech (i.e. a disjoined exception), and (تكونَ) means "تَقَعُ" (occurs) and is of the kind of "kāna" that does not need a khabar (predicate); that is why "تِجارة" was put in the nominative. [Translator's note: the verse is quoted first with the accusative تِجَارَةً, the reading of the Kufans, and then with the nominative تِجَارَةٌ, which the explanation addresses.]

akhfash:31-31.t:
He said ﴿وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ مُّدْخَلاً كَرِيماً﴾ because it is from "أَدْخَلَ", "يُدْخِلُ"; the noun of place from this has ḍamma on the mīm, because it is likened to the quadriliteral verbs, "دحرج" and the like. Do you not see that you say "هذا مُدَحْرَجُنا" (this is our rolling-place)? So when the verb exceeds three letters, the mīm takes ḍamma. Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and seventy-first shāhid]:
الحَمْدُ للّهِ مُمْسانا وَمُصْبَحنَا * بِالْخَيْرِ صَبَّحنا رَبِّي وَمَسَّانا
(Praise be to Allah at our evening and our morning; with good my Lord brought us the morning and the evening.)
because it is from "أمْسى"* and "أَصْبَحَ". And He said ﴿رَّبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ﴾. The mīm may take fatḥa, if you wish, when you derive it from "دَخَل" and "خَرَج". And He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ﴾ when you derive it from "قاَم", "يَقوم"; if you derive it from "أَقامَ", "يُقِيمُ", you say "مُقامٍ أَمين".

akhfash:32-32.t:
He said ﴿وَلاَ تَتَمَنَّوْاْ﴾: if you wish, you assimilate the first tāʾ into the second. If it is asked: how can it be assimilated, when, if you assimilate it, it becomes unvowelled while before it is the unvowelled alif of "لا", so that you combine two unvowelled letters? I say: this alif is a soft letter (ḥarf līn). Assimilation may occur after the like of it, both within a word and otherwise, e.g. "يضربانّي" [and] ﴿فَلاَ تّنَاجَوْاْ بِٱلإِثْمِ وَٱلْعُدْوَانِ﴾ — you may also assimilate it — and like it is ﴿قُلْ أَتُحَآجُّونّا فِي اللَّهِ﴾, where you assimilate although an unvowelled wāw precedes it. And if you wish, you do not assimilate any of this.
Some of the readers read ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونِ﴾, meaning ﴿تُبَشِّرُونَنِي﴾: one of the two nūns was dropped because their combination is found heavy, just as they say "ما أَحسَسْتُ مِنْهُمْ أَحدا" (I did not perceive anyone of them) [as "أَحَسْتُ"], dropping one of the two sīns because it is found heavy. This one [the two nūns] is more deserving of being found heavy, because both are vowelled. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and seventy-second shāhid]:
تَراهُ كالثُّغَامِ يُعَلُّ مِسْكاً * يَسُوءُ الفالِياتِ إِذَا فَلَيْنِي
(You see it [my hair] like white thughām plants, drenched again and again with musk; it grieves the women who search it for lice when they search me.)
He dropped the latter nūn, because it is the nūn that is added so that what precedes it is left in its state, and it is not a noun [pronoun]. As for the first, it may not be dropped, because it is the implied noun [the pronoun]. And Abū Ḥayya al-Numayrī said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and seventy-third shāhid]:
أبِالموتِ الذي لا بُدَّ أَنِّي * مُلاقٍ - لا أَبَاكِ - تُخَوِّفِيني
(Is it with death, which I must inevitably meet — you fatherless one! — that you frighten me?)
So he dropped the nūn. If ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونِّ﴾ were read with a doubled nūn, it would be good, though I have not heard it — as if the nūn were assimilated and the yāʾ dropped, as it is dropped at verse endings, e.g. ﴿بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِ﴾, meaning "عذابي" (My punishment).
As for His saying ﴿فَظِلتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾, its first letter has kasra only because one says "ظَلِلْتُ"; when one of the two letters went because of heaviness, its vowel was transferred to the ẓāʾ. Aws ibn Maghrāʾ said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and seventy-fourth shāhid]:
مِسْنَا السَّماءَ فَنِلْناها وَطَالَهُمُ * حَتَّى رَأَوْا أُحُداً يَهْوِي وَثَهْلانا
(We touched the sky and reached it, and it rose above them, until they saw Uḥud and Thahlān falling down.)
because it is from "مَسَسْتُ". Some read ﴿ فَظَلْتُم﴾, leaving the ẓāʾ with its fatḥa and dropping one of the two lāms; whoever says this says "مَسْنا السماءَ". This dropping* is not regular; it is dropped only in these particular letters I have mentioned to you, and it is dropped only where the final radical (lām al-fiʿl) of the verb is not vowelled; where the final radical is vowelled, there is no dropping.

akhfash:35-35.t: He said ﴿شِقَاقَ بَيْنِهِمَا﴾, putting it in iḍāfa (genitive construct) with "البَيْن", because it may be a noun. He said ﴿لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنُكُمْ﴾ with ḍamma. Had He said ﴿شِقَاقاً بَيْنَهما﴾ in [ordinary] speech, making "البَيْن" an adverb (ẓarf), it would be permissible and good. And if you said ﴿شِقاقَ بينَهما﴾ meaning ﴿ما﴾ and dropping it, it would be permissible, just as you say ﴿تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ meaning the ﴿ما﴾ that has the sense of "thing". And He said ﴿تَعَالَوْاْ إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَآءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾. You say "بينَهُما بَوْنٌ بَعِيدٌ" (between them is a great distance), putting it with wāw, whereas that one [بَيْن] is with yāʾ. And one also says "بينَهما بَيْنٌ بَعيدٌ" with yāʾ.

akhfash:36-36.t:
He said ﴿وَٱلْجَارِ ٱلْجُنُبِ﴾, and some read ﴿الجَنْبِ﴾. The rajaz poet said [this is the one hundred and seventy-fifth shāhid]:
* الناسُ جَنْبٌ والأَمِيرُ جَنْبُ *
(The people are on one side and the governor is on [another] side.)
By "جَنْب" he means: the side. This is the one remote from kinship, which is why He said "جَنِبٌ"; and "الجُنُبُ" too is the one apart from kinship; and "الجانِبُ" is also said.
As for ﴿َٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلجَنْبِ﴾, its meaning is: "the one who is at your side", as you say "فلان بجنبي" (so-and-so is at my side) and "إلى جنبي" (next to me).

akhfash:39-39.t: He said ﴿وَمَاذَا عَلَيْهِمْ لَوْ آمَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ﴾: if you wish, you take ﴿ماذا﴾ as having the status of "ما" alone, and if you wish, you take ﴿ذا﴾ as having the status of "الذي" (that which).

akhfash:42-42.t:
He said ﴿وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثاً﴾, i.e. the limbs will not conceal it; or He means: "it will not be hidden from Him even if they conceal it".
And He said ﴿لَوْ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلأَرْضُ﴾, and some read ﴿تَسَوَّىَ﴾, [and] both are good.

akhfash:43-43.t:
His saying ﴿وَلاَ جُنُباً﴾ is singular in form and is likewise used for the plural, and likewise for men and women, as He said ﴿وَالْمَلاَئِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ﴾, making "الظَهير" (supporter) singular. The Arabs say "هُمْ لِي صَدِيقٌ" (they are a friend to me). And He said ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾, though they are two seated [recorders]. And He said ﴿إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ 
 and He said ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِيۤ﴾, because "فَعُول" and "فَعِيل" are among the patterns used in the singular for the dual and the plural.
And He said ﴿وَلاَ جُنُباً إِلاَّ عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ﴾ because He had said ﴿لاَ تَقْرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ﴾: His saying ﴿وأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), so He said ﴿وَلاَ جُنُباً﴾ by conjunction (ʿaṭf), as if He said: "and do not approach it in a state of janāba, except as travellers on the road", as you say "لا تَأْتِي إِلاّ رَاكِباً" (do not come except riding).

akhfash:46-46.t:
He said ﴿مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِ﴾, meaning "among them is a group (قَوْمٌ)", so "القَوْم" is left implied. al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and seventy-sixth shāhid]:
كَأَنَّكَ منْ جِمالِ بَنِي أُقَيْشٍ * يُقَعْقَعُ بَيْنَ رِجْلَيْهِ بِشَنِّ
(As if you were one of the camels of the Banū Uqaysh, with a dry water-skin rattled between its legs.)
i.e. as if you were a camel of them. And as He said ﴿وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ إِلاَّ لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ﴾, i.e. "and there is not one of them but will surely believe in him". The Arabs say "رَأيتُ الذي أَمْسِ", i.e. "I saw the one who came to you yesterday" or "who spoke yesterday".
﴿وَٱسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ وَرَاعِنَا لَيّاً ﴾: His saying ﴿رَاعِنَا﴾ means "lend us your hearing", in the sense of "أَرِعْنا". And His saying ﴿غَيْرَ مُسْمِعٍ﴾ means "may I not hear", i.e. "may you not be heard"; and as for ﴿غَيْرَ مُسْمِعٍ﴾, it means: nothing is heard from you, so you are "not made to be heard". [Translator's note: the quotation has «مُسْمَعٍ» once and «مُسْمِعٍ» twice; translated as written.]
And He said ﴿وَٱسْمَعْ وَٱنْظُرْنَا لَكَانَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ﴾. He said ﴿وَٱنْظُرْنَا﴾ only because it is from "نَظَرْتُه", i.e. "انْتَظَرْتُهُ" (I waited for him). And He said ﴿ٱنظُرُونَا نَقْتَبِسْ مِن نُّورِكُمْ﴾, i.e. wait for us. As for His saying ﴿يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ﴾, it is only "[he looks] at (إلى) what his hands have sent forth". The poet said:
[in the khafīf metre; this is the one hundred and seventy-seventh shāhid]
ظاهِراتُ الجَمالِ والحُسْنِ يَنْظُرْ * نَ كَما تَنْظُرُ الأَراكَ الظِّباءُ
(Of manifest beauty and loveliness, they look as gazelles look at the arāk trees.)
And if you wish, ﴿يَنْظُرُ المَرْءُ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ﴾ is interrogative, like your saying "he looks [to see] whether it is good that his hands have sent forth or evil".

akhfash:47-47.t: He said ﴿يَا أَيُّهَآ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾ up to His saying ﴿مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّطْمِسَ وُجُوهاً﴾, meaning: before the Day of Resurrection.

akhfash:55-55.t: He said ﴿وَكَفَىٰ بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيراً﴾: this is like "دَهِين" (oiled) and "صَرِيع" (felled) [i.e. faʿīl in the sense of a passive participle], because you say "سُعِرَتْ" (it was kindled), so "هِيَ مَسْعُورَةٌ" (it is kindled). And He said ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ﴾.

akhfash:56-56.t: He said ﴿بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَهَا لِيَذُوقُواْ ٱلْعَذَابَ﴾. If someone says: "Is it not only the skins that sinned that are punished? So how does He say ﴿غَيْرَهَا﴾ (other than them)?" I say: The Arabs may say "أَصوُغُ خَاتَماً غيرَ ذا" (I will fashion a ring other than this one), and he breaks it and then fashions it in another fashioning; so it is the first one, except that the fashioning has changed.

akhfash:65-65.t: And He said ﴿وَيُسَلِّمُواْ تَسْلِيماً﴾, i.e. ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ﴾ and until ﴿يُسَلِّمُوا﴾; all of this is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what follows "حتى".

akhfash:66-66.t: He said ﴿مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ﴾, putting ﴿قَلِيلٌ﴾ in the nominative because you have assigned the verb to them and made them a badal (substitute) from the pronouns implied in the verb.

akhfash:69-69.t: He said ﴿وَحَسُنَ أُولَـٰئِكَ رَفِيقاً﴾. This is not on the pattern of "نِعْمَ الرَّجُل" (what an excellent man), because "نِعْمَ" only falls on a noun with alif and lām or an indefinite noun; rather this is like your saying "كَرُمَ زَيْدٌ رَجُلاً" (how noble Zayd is as a man), which you put in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). And "الرَفِيقُ" (companion) is singular with a plural meaning, like "هُمْ لي صَدِيقٌ" (they are a friend to me).

akhfash:72-72.t: He said ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ﴾: the first lām has fatḥa because it is for emphasis, as in "إنَّ في الدّارِ لَزَيْداً" (indeed in the house is Zayd), and the second lām is for the oath, as if He said: "and among you is one who — by Allah — will surely lag behind".

akhfash:74-74.t: He said ﴿فَلْيُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشْرُونَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾, and He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ﴾, i.e. sells it. So "شَرَيْتُ" may be used for selling and for buying.

akhfash:75-75.t: He said ﴿مِنْ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا﴾. You put "الظالِم" in the genitive because it is a qualifier placed before [its subject], what precedes it is genitive, and it belongs to something connected with the first [noun] (sababī); when it is so, it follows the first in the genitive until it becomes as if it were its own [qualifier].

akhfash:79-79.t: He said ﴿وَمَآ أَصَابَكَ مِن سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِن نَّفْسِكَ وَأَرْسَلْنَاكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولاً﴾. He put the khabar (predicate) with fāʾ because ﴿مَا﴾ has the status of ﴿مَنْ﴾. And He put ﴿مِنْ﴾ before "the evil" because ﴿ما﴾ is negation, and ﴿مِن﴾ is good in negation, as in your saying "ما جاءَنِي من أحد" (no one at all came to me). [Translator's note: here ﴿مَا﴾ is described as negation, although it was just treated as having the status of ﴿مَنْ﴾ (conditional/relative); translated as written.]

akhfash:81-81.t: He said ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ طَاعَةٌ فَإِذَا بَرَزُواْ مِنْ عِندِكَ بَيَّتَ طَآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُمْ﴾, i.e. and they say "our affair is obedience". If you wish, you put "الطاعة" in the accusative on [the implied] "we obey with obedience". And He said ﴿بَيَّتَ﴾, putting the verb of "الطائفة" (the party) in the masculine, because in meaning they are men, and He has attached it [by iḍāfa, "of them"] to masculine [persons]. And He said ﴿وَإِن كَانَ طَآئِفَةٌ مَّنكُمْ﴾.

akhfash:83-83.t: He said ﴿لاَتَّبَعْتُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾: [the exception] goes back to ﴿وَإِذَا جَآءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَمْنِ أَوِ ٱلْخَوْفِ أَذَاعُواْ بِهِ﴾ ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.

akhfash:84-84.t: He said ﴿فَقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لاَ تُكَلَّفُ إِلاَّ نَفْسَكَ﴾ — jussive (jazm) as the answer to the imperative. Some put it in the nominative as a new start (ibtidāʾ), not making it a consequence of the first; and that is how we read it — as He said ﴿وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِٱلصَّلاَةِ وَٱصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لاَ نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقاً﴾: jussive if He made it a consequence of what precedes, and nominative as a new start; and we read it in the nominative.

akhfash:88-88.t: He said ﴿فَمَا لَكُمْ فِي ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ﴾, putting it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as you say "مالَكَ قائما" (what is the matter with you, standing?), i.e. "what is the matter with you in the state of standing?".

akhfash:90-90.t: He said ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِّيثَاقٌ أَوْ جَآءُوكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ﴾, or ﴿حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ﴾. (حَصِرَةً) is a noun which you put in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and ﴿حَصِرَتْ﴾ is [a verb on the pattern] "فَعِلَتْ"; and that is how we read it. [Translator's note: the second quotation was evidently meant to give the variant reading «حَصِرَةً صُدُورُهُمْ», which the explanation discusses; the text repeats ﴿حَصِرَتْ﴾.]

akhfash:92-92.t:
He said ﴿فَدِيَةٌ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىۤ أَهْلِهِ وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةً﴾.
And He said ﴿فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ﴾, i.e. then that is incumbent on him.
And He said ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَصَّدَّقُواْ﴾: that is incumbent on you, unless they remit it as charity*.

akhfash:94-94.t: He said ﴿إِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُواْ﴾, and some read ﴿فَتَثَبَّتُوا﴾. Both are correct, because you say "تَبَيَّنْ حالَ القَوْمِ" (ascertain the state of the people) and "تَثَبَّتْ" (verify), and "لا تُقْدِمْ حَتَّى تَتَبَيَّنْ" (do not advance until you ascertain) and "حَتّى تَتَثَبَّتْ" (until you verify).

akhfash:95-95.t: He said ﴿لاَّ يَسْتَوِي ٱلْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ غَيْرُ أُوْلِي ٱلضَّرَرِ﴾ — nominative, because you have made it a qualifier of "القاعدين" (those who sit back). If you put it in the genitive, it is [as a qualifier] of "المُؤْمِنِين". And if you wish, you put it in the accusative when you take it out of the beginning of the speech and make it an exception; and that is how we read it. It has reached us that it was revealed after His saying ﴿لاَّ يَسْتَوِي ٱلْقَاعِدُونَ﴾ and was not revealed with it; it is only an exception by which He meant people who were unable to go out [to fight]. Then He said ﴿وَٱلْمُجَاهِدُونَ﴾, conjoining it to "القاعدين", because the meaning is ﴿لاَّ يَسْتَوِي ٱلْقَاعِدُونَ﴾ ﴿وَٱلْمُجَاهِدُونَ﴾. And He said ﴿وَفَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُجَاهِدِينَ عَلَى ٱلْقَاعِدِينَ أَجْراً عَظِيماً﴾ ﴿دَرَجَاتٍ مِّنْهُ﴾, meaning: He did that, [in] ranks from Him. And He said ﴿أَجْراً عَظِيماً﴾ because He said "He preferred them", so He has informed [us] that He rewarded them, and He spoke according to that meaning, like your saying "أمَا وَاللّهِ لأَضْرِبَنَكَ إيجاعاً شَدِيداً" (by Allah, I will surely beat you with a severe hurting), because its meaning is: I will surely hurt you.

akhfash:97-97.t: [And] He said ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَسَآءَتْ مَصِيراً﴾ ﴿ إِلاَّ ٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾, because He excepted them from them, as you say "أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُكَ إِلاّ زَيْداً" (those are your companions except Zayd) and "كُلُّهُم أَصْحابُكَ إِلاّ زيداً" (all of them are your companions except Zayd). It is outside [the scope of] the beginning of the speech.

akhfash:104-104.t: He said ﴿إِن تَكُونُواْ تَأْلَمُونَ﴾, i.e. you are in pain (تَيْجَعُون). You say "ألِمَ", "يَأْلَمُ", "أَلَما".

akhfash:109-109.t: He said ﴿هَا أَنْتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ جَادَلْتُمْ عَنْهُمْ﴾: He repeated the [particle of] drawing attention (tanbīh) twice, as He said ﴿هَا أَنتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ تُدْعَوْنَ﴾; He intended emphasis.

akhfash:114-114.t: [And] He said ﴿لاَّ خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّن نَّجْوَاهُمْ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ﴾, meaning: "except in the secret talk of one who enjoins charity".

akhfash:131-131.t: He said ﴿وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنِ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ﴾, i.e. "that (بأَنْ) you fear Allah".

akhfash:134-134.t:
[And He said] ﴿مَّن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا فَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ ثَوَابُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾: the position of ﴿كَانَ﴾ is jussive, the answer is with fāʾ, and ﴿يُرِيدُ﴾ is nominative because there is no conjunction in it [linking it to the jussive]. As He said ﴿مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾, and He said ﴿مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ ٱلآخِرَةِ نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ وَمَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ ٱلدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا﴾ — He used the jussive [in the answer] because the first is in the position of the jussive, but it is a past (affirmed) verb and so does not take the jussive [form]; and ﴿يُرِيدُ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿كَانَ﴾.
[And] He said ﴿وَإِنِ ٱمْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِن بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزاً أَوْ إِعْرَاضاً﴾, letting the noun come right after ﴿إنْ﴾, because it is the most firmly established of the conditional particles. This is only good with it when the form of what it governs is not jussive, as in his saying [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and seventy-eighth shāhid]:
* عاوِدْ هَراةَ وإِنْ مَعْمُورُها خَرَبا *
(Return to Herat, even if its inhabited part has fallen into ruin.)

akhfash:135-135.t:
He said ﴿إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقَيراً فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا﴾, because ﴿أوْ﴾ here has the meaning of wāw (and). Or [the dual] in His saying ﴿بِهِما﴾ combines them because both have been mentioned, as in the saying of [Allah] the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا﴾. Or ﴿مَنْ﴾ is left implied, as if it were "if the one who disputes is rich or poor", meaning "two rich or two poor", taking "مَنْ" in that meaning while ﴿غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقَيراً﴾ comes out according to the [singular] form of "مَنْ".
And He said ﴿وَإِن* تَلْوُواْ أَوْ تُعْرِضُواْ﴾, because it is from "لَوى", "يَلْوِى" (to twist). Some read ﴿وإِنْ تَلُوا﴾: if it is a dialect usage, it is because of the meeting of the two wāws; but I consider it nothing but a solecism (laḥn), except in the sense of "الوِلاية" (taking charge), and "الوِلايَة" has no meaning here except in the sense of "وإِنْ تَلُوا عَلَيْهِم" (if you take charge over them), with ﴿عَلَيْهِم﴾ dropped — then it is permissible.

akhfash:148-148.t: He said ﴿لاَّ يُحِبُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْجَهْرَ بِٱلسُّوۤءِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ﴾, because when He said ﴿لاَّ يُحِبُّ ٱللَّهُ﴾ He informed [us] that it is not lawful. Then He said ﴿إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ﴾: it is lawful for him to speak evil aloud of the one who wronged him. Some read ﴿ظَلَم﴾ [active], [taking it] with His saying ﴿مَّا يَفْعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمْ﴾, [so that] ﴿إِلاَّ مَن ظَلَم﴾ [would have the sense of] "except by punishing the one who did wrong".

akhfash:155-155.t: He said ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مَّيثَاقَهُمْ﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is zāʾida (redundant), as if He said "فبنقضهم" (so for their breaking).

akhfash:156-156.t: ﴿وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ وَقَوْلِهِمْ عَلَىٰ مَرْيَمَ﴾ ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا ٱلْمَسِيحَ﴾ — all of it is [conjoined] to the first.

akhfash:164-164.t:
[And] He said ﴿وَرُسُلاً قَدْ قَصَصْنَاهُمْ عَلَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: it is in the accusative because the verb has been occupied with something connected to it [i.e. the pronoun], and what precedes it is in the accusative by a verb.
[And] ﴿وَكَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ مُوسَىٰ تَكْلِيماً﴾: the speech is a creation from Allah, not like speech from you and not in the way it comes from you; Allah created it and then conveyed it to Moses. [Translator's note: this is the author's own theological position, translated as written.]

akhfash:170-170.t:
[And] He said ﴿فَآمِنُواْ خَيْراً لَّكُمْ﴾, putting ﴿خَيْراً لَكُمْ﴾ in the accusative because when He said to them ﴿آمِنُواْ﴾ He commanded them to do what is better for them, so it is as if He said: "do what is better for you". Likewise ﴿ٱنتَهُواْ خَيْراً لَّكُمْ﴾. This occurs only in command and prohibition specifically and does not occur in statements, because in command and prohibition [the verb] is not left implied [otherwise], and it is as if you moved it from one thing to another. The poet said [in the sarīʿ metre; this is the one hundred and seventy-ninth shāhid]:
فَفواعِديه سَرْحَتَيْ مالِكٍ * أو الرُّبا بَينَهُما أسَهْلا
(So make an appointment with him at the two trees of Mālik, or the hillocks between them — [that is] easier.)
just as you say "واعديه خيراً لك" (make an appointment with him — [that is] better for you). I have heard the accusative of this in statements too; the Arabs say "آتى البيتَ خيراً لي" (I will come to the house — [that is] better for me) and "أتركُهُ خيراً لي" (I will leave it — [that is] better for me), and it is according to what I explained for command and prohibition.

akhfash:176-176.t: He said ﴿إِن ٱمْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ﴾, like ﴿وَإِنِ ٱمْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ﴾; the explanation of both is the same.
